newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso heads to Europe to drum up trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso heads to Europe to drum up trade.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso travels to Britain and Italy on Saturday to raise trade concerns and sell Latin America's largest country to potential European investors, diplomats said.

Marcelo Andrade de Moraes Jardim, director general of the Brazilian Foreign Ministry's Europe Department, said Cardoso would be the main speaker at a two-day conference in London on Feb. 9-10 called "Link into Latin America."
"The president will explain where Brazil is, the transformations it has gone through and the leaps it has made," Jardim told reporters.

In both Britain and Italy, which Cardoso will visit on Feb. 11-14, the Brazilian leader will lobby for a greater opening of the European Union's market to Brazilian goods, especially agricultural products.

"The president no doubt will make our interest plain in having these countries as allies in areas where we are at odds with the European Union," Jardim said, citing what he said were EU trade barriers to orange juice and chicken exports.

Jornal do Brasil economic columnist Guilherme Barros put it more bluntly. "One of the high points of Cardoso's speech on Monday in London will be an attack on the difficulties Brazilian agricultural products face in entering the European market," he wrote, citing EU subsidies in particular.

Trade concerns have increasingly become an issue in Brazil, which posted a record trade gap last year of $5.5 billion, expected to grow this year to at least $8.0 billion. In recent weeks, Brazilian officials have picked a fight with Washington over what they see as unfair barriers to Brazilian orange juice and metals exports.

At the same time, Brazil has been deflecting U.S. calls for it to open its promising telecommunications market faster and to join an international agreement on ending tariffs on information technology trade.
In London, Cardoso will meet Prime Minister John Major and leaders of the opposition Labour and Liberal Democrat parties.

n Italy, Cardoso will meet President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro and be awarded an honorary degree by Bologna university. He will also pay the first official state visit by a Brazilian leader to the Vatican, where he will have an audience with Pope John Paul II.
